failures.problem: Valid public CharSpace/CharKern tables were rejected in JAM2, causing an explicit illegal instruction at FFAA5E and then exception-stack corruption.
failures.fix: Build and draw a complete monochrome scanline template in each draw mode, using native pen-movement bounds and optional signed metrics.

failures.problem: Legacy expanded emitter skipped leading negative kerning and required unrelated font/glyph storage for a metrics-only query.
failures.fix: Direct optional-metric walker, full unsigned low-16-bit count and native WORD result, without marker, glyph storage or proportional-flag requirements.

failures.problem: The native emitter left IntuiText pens and DrawMode in the caller RasterPort.
failures.fix: Restore caller foreground/background pens and drawing mode after the chain; leave the final cursor updated as native does.

failures.problem: A beam-spin WaitTOF repeatedly runs inside the ROM IRQ transaction guard; in Frozen mode a higher-priority input task remains READY while the game continues polling beam routines. F8 and B no longer receive useful input. The message pool is not full and modifiers are released.
failures.fix: Use native SIGF_SINGLE ($10), suspend via Exec Wait, and wake from a stack-owned VBlank tail server; remove Exec library/task metadata legitimacy checks. Keep the compiled main and private transaction guard unchanged.

mouseFailure.observation: Selecting the first engine at window position 200,8 returns to the depot instead of the car list. CopperStart exposes identical global/window mouse units on a low-resolution screen; native uses doubled global units.
mouseFailure.nativeCause: On the low-resolution game screen, global Intuition coordinates must be twice the screen/window pixel coordinates. The game halves its global X; the old maximum 319 cannot reach the engine picker right-hand hit area.
mouseFailure.finalCorrection: Default raw motion is scaled by two into fixed high-resolution/interlaced global units; per-screen public mouse fields and messages then convert to screen pixels. Physical sprite coordinates use half global units.
